name: Banded Shoulder Prep — Seven Positions, ~2 Minutes
description:
**The shoulder anchor, detached from kettlebell day so it can happen anywhere.**

It has lived inside the KB sessions since the program started, which was fine while those ran weekly — but when the KB days get skipped, this goes with them, and this is the input that has kept the right shoulder quiet through a heavy pressing block.

**Seven positions, one round, about two minutes.** No bell, no bench, just a light band. Run it on a rest day, after a swim, before a gym session, or on the floor of the apartment gym.

**Push and pull days deliberately do NOT carry extra band volume** — those days already run long and have their own anchors (Yuri's on push, band-pull-apart on pull). This is for the days that have neither.

anytime.label: Banded Shoulder Prep
anytime.note: Seven positions, ~2 min, light band. Any day, before or after.

sets.name: Banded Shoulder Prep (~2 min)
sets.notes:
One round of all seven, about two minutes. **Sustained tension, no rest between positions.**

**Tired-day version:** 6 reps each. Exhausted: do it anyway at whatever range stays smooth — a small clean range beats a big ragged one.

**Seated is the default** because it takes the legs and the low back out of it, but standing is fine if that is what is available.

exercises.notes: Arms overhead, pull apart without letting the ribs flare.
Slow and controlled. Blades down and together.
Thumbs up, arms to a T. Traps stay quiet.
Rear delts. Lead with the elbows.
Hold the V overhead. Ribs down, shoulders packed.

tips: Two minutes, one round, light band. Sustained tension beats heavy tension.
This is why the right shoulder has stayed quiet — it works because it is frequent, not because it is hard.
Tired-day version is 6 reps each. Do it badly rather than skip it.
Don't add this on top of push or pull day — those already have their own shoulder anchor.
